content.text: {"relation":"MATCH","consensus_summary":"The blind consensus recognizes 'seed' as a richly multivalent symbol with two leading strands: (1) the Word of God/gospel sown in human hearts (grounded in Jesus' own explicit interpretation, Luke 8:11), and (2) offspring/descendants culminating messianically in Christ (Gen 3:15; Gal 3:16). Responses A and C list the Word-of-God sense as primary; B and D list the messianic-offspring sense as primary but treat the Word-of-God sense as dominant or common. Secondary strands include death/resurrection, sowing-reaping, faith, kingdom growth, and regeneration.","book_summary":"The book defines seed simply as 'the word of God, sown in the hearts of men,' citing Luke 8:11 and cross-referencing 'Grass.'","consensus_core_identification":"Seed symbolizes, at its most authoritative and widely taught level, the Word of God/gospel sown into human hearts (with the messianic-offspring sense as a co-leading strand in redemptive-historical contexts).","book_core_identification":"Seed = the word of God sown in human hearts.","core_relation":"EQUIVALENT","extension_relation":"BOOK_SUBSET","boundary_disagreement":"The book presents only the parabolic Word-of-God sense and is silent on the other consensus strands (messianic offspring, death/resurrection, faith, sowing-reaping). This is omission rather than rejection: a terse glossary entry that gives one sense without denying others does not constitute a boundary dispute. If the book's single definition were read as exhaustive, it would exclude the offspring/Christ cases (Gen 3:15; Gal 3:16) that half the consensus responses rank as primary, but nothing in the entry asserts exclusivity.","material_contradiction":"None. The book's identification is verbatim the interpretation Scripture itself supplies (Luke 8:11) and is listed as primary or dominant in all four consensus responses.","rationale":"The book's core identification is exactly the strand two consensus responses name as primary and the other two rank as their leading alternative ('dominant'). Since the consensus explicitly treats the Word-of-God sense as having the strongest claim to consensus status because Jesus himself defines it that way, the book's entry is equivalent to the consensus core. The narrower coverage of the glossary entry (ignoring the messianic-offspring track) is a subset by silence, not a material redrawing of boundaries, so REFINED is not warranted.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"Two of the four consensus responses (B and D) rank the messianic-offspring sense as primary, so one could argue the book, by presenting only the Word-of-God sense, implicitly demotes or excludes what a substantial portion of interpreters consider the theologically central meaning of 'seed,' which might merit REFINED (narrowing) rather than MATCH.","confidence":"high"}
